\item
  The proper level of salaries for public officials is often a matter of debate. In many countries, public officials supplement their incomes by performing other duties. In the United States, Congressmen deliver lectures for pay and former bureaucrats cash in on their connections by becoming high-paid lobbyists. Recent U.S. proposals call for tying pay increases to limits on these activities. Discuss the efficacy of such a plan.
